title: Introduce protocol-level sampling hints to reduce tracing hotpath overhead
creator: Rajesh Patel
description: Background: Current tracing sampling logic runs expensive checks on the hot request path (allocations for span marshaling, header inspection, content scans) which adds measurable CPU and tail latency under high QPS. Goal: reduce per-request overhead by moving inexpensive, probabilistic ‘sampling hints’ generation to the ingress layer and short-circuiting the heavy sampling decision in downstream services. The hints are intentionally coarse (binary hints + confidence score) and should allow the hotpath to avoid allocations and complex heuristics for the vast majority of requests. This ticket implements the protocol-level hint, runtime support to consume it, rollout plan, and validation dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress adds X-RW-SAMP-HINT header for candidate requests with values: none | likely | force
Services consult header and take O(1) fast-path to either avoid tracing or mark span as low-cost (no payload capture), reducing hotpath allocations
CPU-per-request for the tracing hotpath reduced by >= 25% in canary traffic compared to baseline
No increase in missed high-value traces for incidents (false negative rate < 2% in held-out error sample)
Feature gated with runtime flag and rolloutable via console canary controls
Instrumentation and dashboard panels created: sampling_hint_rate, hint_accuracy_v_errors, tracing_cpu_overhead, full_span_capture_rate
comments: 2026-03-12 Rajesh Patel: Created ticket after spike showed ~18% CPU from trace hotpath during peak. See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Protocol-Level+Sampling+Hints

2026-03-13 Lena Park: Prototype implemented in ingress-proxy (fast Bloom filter + tiny path heuristic). Microbenchmarks: header add cost ~120ns; decision cost in downstream reduced by ~160us for simple endpoints. Pushed branch runtime/ingress/hint-probe. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/pull/423

2026-03-13 Miguel Ortega (review): Nice microbench numbers. Suggest adding a per-tenant budget token check at ingress to keep fair sampling across noisy tenants. Also: need to ensure header cannot be forged in Private deployments (consider HMAC or signed hints).

2026-03-14 Lena Park: Added per-tenant leaky-bucket check to prototype. Put security_review_required=false for hosted, but added note for Private to require signature verification. Updated implementation branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7890

2026-03-14 Rajesh Patel: Planned rollout: 0.1% internal canary -> 1% customer beta -> 10% -> 100% across non-critical routes. Create dashboards and alerts before canary. Assigned to Observability infra for dashboarding (ENG-99721 will track dashboard work).
notes: Tradeoffs: Hints will occasionally misclassify; to mitigate we keep a small random sample of requests where hint==none but still collect full spans. Header trust model differs across deployment modes — hosted will trust ingress, private deployments will need signed hints or local-only hint generation. Should limit header size and keep semantics minimal to avoid downstream parsing cost.
implementation_steps: Add hint generator to ingress-proxy with configurable heuristics and per-tenant token bucket
Add fast-path consumer in tracing library to consult X-RW-SAMP-HINT and avoid allocations
Add fallback random sampling for a small percentage to measure missed-critical-traces
Add dashboards, SLO/alert for hint_accuracy_v_errors and tracing_cpu_overhead
Canary rollout and validate performance/accuracy metrics
Document security considerations and add private deployment signature option
